title: The schema-migration tests run a replica of migrateSchema written inside each test, and their "production module" cases only check exports and columns on whatever DB the module bound (before the rails: the already-migrated live DB), so a broken migration step in db.ts stays green

evidence.note: "replicate the production migration steps against an in-memory DB": applyV1Migration .. applyV7Migration are written in the test
production cases: import src/utils/db and assert user_version 7 and two column names on the module's own DB
Test 5 prepares its own copy of the markExitFailedHeld SQL ("markExitFailedHeld production SQL")
"Production migrateSchema() replica ... mirrors the structure of src/utils/db.ts:29-123" (migrateSchema ends at :232 at the base SHA)
Test 6 prepares its own setPauseState SQL
the real migrateSchema, run only at module import
the v6 to v7 step that the exit_failed_held persistence depends on

sibling_sites_checked: All three db/*Migration.test.ts files follow the same replica + "production module integration" pattern; anti-rug/dryRunTimestamp.test.ts copies one statement (AUD-TESTU-010); db.test.ts copies the risk SQL (AUD-TESTU-017). No unit test opens a fresh temp DB through the real module and checks the upgrade path from an older version.
severity_rationale: S2: the migrations carry state the exit engine relies on (exit_failed_held, pause_state, lp_baseline); a broken upgrade step loses failed-held persistence (an S1 stranded-position class) while the replicas stay green. The production cases add live-DB reach before the rails (AUD-TESTU-001).
recommendation: Phase 28: run the real migration (dbSchema.ts after the 22-09 move) against temp DBs seeded at v4, v5 and v6, then assert the schema and run the real prepared statements; delete the replicas.
affected_cases: exitFailedHeldMigration: production user_version pragma reports 7 after module load
pauseStateMigration: Tests 1-10 (replica migration and own statements)
escaped_regression: Delete the ALTER TABLE exit_state ADD COLUMN exit_status guard from the version < 7 step at src/utils/db.ts:194: a fresh or v6 DB never gets the column (markExitFailedHeld then throws on every still-held failed exit), while the replica tests stay green and the production cases stay green on any DB that already had the column (the live DB before the rails).
